chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Lu'lu'i from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Abu Jamilah from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about those in ihram who caught young ostriches, slaughtered them, and ate them. He said: 'Upon them is, for every young ostrich they caught and ate, a camel, which they share among themselves; they calculate based on the number of young ostriches and the number of men.' I said: 'Among them is one who cannot afford anything.' He said: 'He evaluates it according to the proportion of the camels, and fasts for each camel eighteen days.'

And if the one in ihram catches two birds, one from the birds of the Haram (sanctuary) and the other from the birds outside the Haram, he buys fodder with the value of the Haram bird to feed the pigeons of the Haram, and gives charity in compensation for the other. Narrated.

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A mature camel used as a unit of compensation
key_terms.مُحْرِمِينَ: Those in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation (fidya) for a pilgrim in ihram who kills an ostrich or birds?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fidya (compensation) for killing game while in ihram, emphasizing the principle of shared liability among the group for a single camel. It further distinguishes between birds of the sacred precinct (Haram) and others, prescribing feeding sanctuary pigeons for the former and general charity for the latter, reflecting the juristic nuance of valuing the sanctity of the location. The provision for those unable to afford the full share to pay the equivalent value and fast highlights the practical flexibility within Shia fiqh to ensure the obligation is met according to one's capacity.
